recipe.name: Dal Fry
steps: Rinse the dal until the water is fairly clear. Simmer with 900 ml water and turmeric for 35–45 minutes, partly covered, until the grains mash easily; stir and check the water level.
Finely chop onion, tomato, ginger and garlic. Heat ghee in a pan, sizzle cumin, then cook onion for 6–8 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute. Add tomato, chilli powder and salt; cook for 8 minutes until soft and the ghee appears at the edges.
Whisk the cooked dal lightly and add to the pan with the remaining 200 ml water. Simmer for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the dal pours thickly from a spoon.
Stir in garam masala and chopped coriander. Taste and serve hot with rice or roti prepared separately; this recipe supplies the dal only.

recipe.name: Chana Dal
steps: Rinse and soak the chana dal in plenty of water for 2 hours, then drain. Chop the tomato, ginger and chilli finely.
Bring the drained dal, turmeric and 1000 ml fresh water to a boil. Simmer partly covered for 45–55 minutes, until tender but still holding its shape.
Heat ghee in another pan and sizzle the cumin. Add ginger and chilli for 1 minute, then tomato, salt and chilli powder; cook for 7–8 minutes until pulpy.
Fold the tempering into the dal with the remaining 100 ml water. Simmer for 5 minutes and finish with coriander; the dal should be tender with a light gravy, not a paste.

recipe.name: Yellow Moong Dal
steps: Rinse the moong dal thoroughly and drain. Put it in a saucepan with 950 ml water and turmeric; bring to a boil and skim any heavy foam.
Simmer partly covered for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the grains collapse when pressed. Whisk briefly for a soft, creamy consistency.
Heat ghee in a small pan and sizzle cumin. Add finely chopped ginger and chilli and stir for 1 minute without browning heavily. Pour the tempering into the dal carefully.
Add salt and the remaining 100 ml water, simmer for 3 minutes, then switch off. Stir in lemon juice and coriander; serve warm with separately prepared rice.

recipe.name: Pindi Chole
steps: Soak chickpeas in plenty of water for 8–12 hours in the refrigerator, then discard the soaking water and rinse. Tie the tea leaves securely in a clean food-safe muslin bag.
Boil chickpeas with the measured fresh water and tea bag, then simmer partly covered for 75–95 minutes until easily crushed. Add hot water if needed to keep them covered. Remove the tea bag.
Drain the chickpeas, saving 250 ml cooking liquid. Toss them with coriander powder, cumin powder, pomegranate powder, amchur, chilli powder, garam masala and salt.
Heat ghee in a wide pan, sizzle cumin seeds, then add sliced ginger and chilli for 1 minute. Add the spiced chickpeas and reserved liquid and cook for 10–12 minutes, turning gently.
Stop when the spices cling to the chickpeas and little free liquid remains. Check that the centres are completely tender and serve with separately prepared bread.

recipe.name: Lobia Masala
steps: Rinse the black-eyed peas, soak for 4–6 hours and drain. Simmer in 1000 ml fresh water for 35–45 minutes until tender all the way through; keep the cooking liquid.
Finely chop the onion, tomato, ginger and garlic. Heat oil, sizzle cumin, and fry onion for 8 minutes until golden. Add ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt. Cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the tomato becomes a thick paste and oil beads at the edges.
Add the cooked peas with their liquid and remaining 200 ml water. Simmer for 10 minutes; mash a spoonful against the pan to thicken the gravy, keeping most peas whole.

recipe.name: Langar wali Dal
steps: Rinse both dals and soak together in plenty of water for 8 hours in the refrigerator. Drain and put in a heavy saucepan with 1500 ml fresh water and turmeric.

steps: Rinse the dal and simmer with turmeric and 950 ml water for 35–45 minutes until soft enough to mash. Stir occasionally and replenish water if the pan becomes dry.

recipe.name: Dhuli Urad Dal
steps: Rinse the urad dal gently, soak for 30 minutes and drain very well. Cut the ginger into fine strips and chop chilli and coriander.
Heat ghee in a wide pan with a lid. Sizzle cumin, add ginger and chilli for 1 minute, then stir in drained dal, turmeric and salt.
Add the measured water, bring to a simmer and cover. Cook on low heat for 18–22 minutes; check gently with a fork and avoid stirring hard, which breaks the grains.
When tender, uncover and evaporate any remaining water over low heat. Rest off heat for 5 minutes, fluff gently and finish with lemon and coriander; the grains should stay separate.

recipe.name: Hare Chane ki Sabzi
steps: Shell and rinse the green chickpeas; the measured weight is for shelled peas. Chop onion and tomato finely and mince ginger and garlic.

recipe.name: Mor Kuzhambu
steps: Soak chana dal and rice for 20 minutes, then drain. Grind with coconut, cumin, green chilli and 100 ml of the measured water to a smooth paste.
Peel and deseed the ash gourd and cut into small cubes. Simmer with 250 ml water, turmeric and salt for 10–12 minutes until translucent and easily pierced.

Turn the heat to its lowest setting and stir in the curd. Heat gently for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until steaming; do not allow a rolling boil or the curd may split.
Heat coconut oil in a small pan, pop mustard seeds and add dried chilli and curry leaves carefully. Pour over the curry, cover briefly and serve with separately cooked rice.

recipe.name: Lemon Coriander Soup
steps: Finely chop the vegetables, ginger and garlic. Wash coriander well; chop the stems separately from the leaves. Mix cornflour with 50 ml of the measured cold water.
Heat oil and soften onion for 3 minutes without browning. Add ginger, garlic and coriander stems for 1 minute, then carrot and cabbage for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining water, salt and pepper. Simmer for 8 minutes until vegetables are tender with a little bite. Stir the slurry again, pour it in and simmer for 2 minutes until lightly glossy.
Turn off the heat and add lemon juice and coriander leaves. Taste and serve immediately; adding lemon at the end keeps the soup bright and fresh.

recipe.name: Manchow Soup
steps: Finely chop cabbage, carrot, capsicum, ginger, garlic and chilli. Separate spring onion whites from greens. Mix cornflour with 60 ml of the measured cold water.
Heat oil in a saucepan. Stir-fry ginger, garlic, chilli and onion whites for 1 minute, then add the remaining chopped vegetables and stir over medium-high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the remaining water, soy sauce, pepper and salt. Simmer for 7 minutes until vegetables are tender but not mushy. Taste before adding any more salt because soy sauce is salty.

Stir the slurry and pour in while mixing. Simmer for 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened, add vinegar and onion greens, then divide into bowls. Add crispy noodles only at serving so they stay crunchy.

recipe.name: Hot and Sour Soup
steps: Cut tofu into narrow strips and shred cabbage and carrot. Chop ginger, garlic, chilli and spring onion, keeping the greens aside. Mix cornflour with 50 ml cold measured water.
Heat oil and stir-fry ginger, garlic, chilli and onion whites for 1 minute. Add carrot and cabbage and cook for 3 minutes, stirring to keep their texture.
Add remaining water, tofu, soy sauce, white pepper and salt. Simmer for 6–8 minutes; stir the slurry again and pour it in while mixing to avoid lumps.

steps: Wash spinach in several changes of water and discard tough stems. Chop spinach, onion, ginger and garlic separately; grit left in the leaves will spoil the smooth soup.

Return to the pan and heat gently. Stir in cream without a hard boil; the shorba should flow freely and coat a spoon lightly. Taste and serve hot.

recipe.name: Pepper Rasam
steps: Soak tamarind in 150 ml warm measured water for 10 minutes. Squeeze and strain, discarding seeds and fibre. Crush pepper, cumin, coriander seeds and peeled garlic coarsely.
Simmer chopped tomato, tamarind extract, turmeric and salt with the remaining water for 8–10 minutes until the tomato is soft and the raw tamarind aroma fades.
Add the crushed spice mixture and simmer for 3–4 minutes. Stop when a light foam rises at the edges; prolonged hard boiling makes the pepper aroma dull.

steps: Rinse toor dal and simmer with turmeric and 450 ml water for 30–40 minutes until completely soft, then mash. Soak tamarind in 150 ml warm water and strain out seeds and fibre.

Heat 5 g of the ghee and roast chana dal, coriander seeds, cumin, pepper and dried chilli over low heat until fragrant. Add coconut and stir until lightly golden, then cool and grind with 100 ml water.
Simmer chopped tomatoes, tamarind extract and salt with the remaining 500 ml water for 8 minutes. Add mashed dal and roasted paste and simmer gently for 5 minutes until aromatic.
Heat the remaining ghee, pop mustard and add curry leaves carefully. Pour into the rasam and finish with coriander; it should be a pourable broth, slightly richer than plain rasam.

steps: Rinse moong dal and simmer with turmeric and 500 ml water for 25 minutes until it breaks down easily. Mash lightly without draining the cooking liquid.

recipe.name: Thukpa
steps: Cut carrot, cabbage and capsicum into thin strips. Chop onion, tomato, ginger and garlic finely. Keep vegetables ready before heating the pan so nothing burns while chopping.
Boil noodles in 1000 ml of the measured water according to the packet until just tender. Drain, discard this cooking water and divide noodles between four deep bowls.
Heat oil and soften onion for 5 minutes. Add ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then tomato, cumin powder and pepper; cook for 5 minutes until tomatoes turn pulpy.
Add the vegetables, remaining 1200 ml water, soy sauce and salt. Simmer for 10–12 minutes until carrot is tender but still holds its shape.
Turn off the heat, stir in lemon juice and coriander and ladle hot broth over noodles. Serve immediately so the noodles do not absorb all the soup.

recipe.name: Dal Shorba
steps: Wash the dal thoroughly. Chop onion, tomato, ginger and garlic finely. Heat ghee in a heavy saucepan and sizzle the cumin without allowing it to blacken.
Cook onion for 5 minutes until softened, then ginger and garlic for 1 minute. Add tomato and turmeric and stir for 4 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
Add dal and water, bring to a boil and simmer partly covered for 25 minutes until dal is very soft. Stir occasionally to prevent the lentils sticking to the bottom.
Cool sufficiently for safe blending and blend until smooth. Return to the pan, add salt and pepper and heat through; the shorba should be thinner than dal for rice.
Take off the heat and stir in lemon juice and coriander. Taste and serve hot in small bowls; reheat any refrigerated portion thoroughly before serving again.
